changes: The official-source snapshot was refreshed on 2026-06-12 UTC across the tracked set.
OpenClaw shipped prerelease v2026.6.6-beta.2 on 2026-06-12 03:32:42 UTC, extending the current beta train two days after v2026.6.6-beta.1 and three days after stable v2026.6.5.
ZeroClaw shipped stable v0.8.0 on 2026-06-12 00:04:32 UTC, which is a real signal that the Rust lightweight lane is still iterating quickly.
PicoClaw posted a fresh nightly build on 2026-06-12 01:35:20 UTC, reinforcing the cheap-hardware / edge-device lane.
The monitored set and taxonomy remain unchanged. Hermes stays canonical at https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent.
whyItMatters: This was a meaningful run because there were actual release-level moves, not just repo churn.
OpenClaw remains the pace-setter. Another beta this quickly after the last stable release is the clearest current sign that the category anchor is still iterating fast in public.
ZeroClaw getting v0.8.0 out the door matters because the strongest lightweight Rust challenger is still shipping, not just accumulating stars.
PicoClaw continues to validate the edge-device narrative, but it does not change the strategic map by itself.
The right move is to refresh the daily layer and hosted dataset, while leaving the stable strategic read unchanged.
